pr_title: fix: allow '.default' to be ignored during schema validation
pr_body:
### What does it do?

- Add 'default' to the list of ignorable attributes's properties
- Sanitize schemas to be valid JSON to make sure no invalid JSON properties are present during the checks

### Why is it needed?

strapi import on identical apps is currently broken because of 'default' not being present all the time

### How to test it?

See #20388 for reproduction

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

fix #20388

This is the first simple fix for this issue.

However, it'll still break transfers using the 'exact' strategy.

`default` is present in the diff because source schemas (extracted from the archive) are stringified then parsed again, whereas the destination ones (taken from the running Strapi instance) still contain invalid JSON properties such as functions (e.g. `default`).

One fix could be to force the programmatic `getSchemas` to return valid JSON data structures (manually excluding the functions & other invalid values)

What do you think? @innerdvations @Bassel17

Yeah, I agree that this works as a quick fix for now, and then the "real" fix should be that `getSchemas` should use the exact same logic as the export method to ensure we don't have any more incongruencies like this.

> Yeah, I agree that this works as a quick fix for now, and then the "real" fix should be that `getSchemas` should use the exact same logic as the export method to ensure we don't have any more incongruencies like this.

Well the fix itself is quite simple (stringify + parse the object that is returned in each Strapi provider's getSchemas). I've tested it and it works well. The question is more: "should we include it in this PR too?"

comments:
Hey Paul, as mentioned in the CLI, since the transfer engine finds discrepancies between source (archive) and destination (app) schemas, it will ignore the related data and only import the rest (permissions, locales, etc...). So, this part is working as intended.

However, the fact that it finds such differences in the schema for the same app (on the `publishedAt.default`) is definitely a bug and is already listed in our internal DX backlog.

Thanks for sharing this, I'll add it to the internal ticket for the reproduction steps.

@Convly thanks for the help, I may be a bit confused.  Why would there be discrepancies if the source was generated from the same app that I am trying to reimport the data too.  Is there a potential fix I can employ to be able to import my data.

@Convly here is a quick repo, just created the app, exported, and tried to import.

![image](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/assets/8593673/756ec85d-870e-43e3-b295-d3c8c19c1ef3)

>Why would there be discrepancies if the source was generated from the same app that I am trying to reimport the data too

That's what I'm saying, there shouldn't be any, it's a known issue with known reproduction steps that we already have in our backlog :slightly_smiling_face:

> Is there a potential fix I can employ to be able to import my data.

Not that I know of, maybe by deleting the schema files in the archive so that the detection isn't run? But I'm not sure it'll accept the source without the schema (you can always try) :thinking:
@Convly thank you for the response.  Yep, I was confused. Now I am not.🙂

review_comments: Do we still need this now that we have the json schema conversion?
We do not necessarily, but if it were to be modified on purpose it still wouldn't make sense to throw because of that.

Basically, we shouldn't have a difference on this field every time (hence the second fix), but if for some reason it happens anyway (user modified their schema), then we should probably ignore it anyway
